raw_response:
Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple, bilateral, peripheral nodular opacities (indicated by arrows), some of which appear to have central lucency or cavitation. This pattern of multiple, well-defined, peripheral pulmonary nodules is the classic radiological presentation of septic pulmonary emboli, often originating from a source like tricuspid valve endocarditis or an infected intravenous catheter. While cavitating metastases can look similar, septic emboli are a more common cause of this specific acute-appearing multifocal pattern in clinical vignettes.
